evaluation:
Helpful Facts:

  • Primary Concern: Headache - Clearly identifies the main reason for the visit.
  • Onset: Approximately 3-4 days ago - Provides a timeframe for the current episode.
  • Quality: Throbbing or pulsing - Characteristic quality often associated with migraine.
  • Location: Typically unilateral - A key feature distinguishing migraine from tension headaches.
  • Timing/Pattern: Intermittent, with periods of relief followed by recurrence - Suggests episodic nature.
  • Exacerbating Factors: Pain exacerbated by movement (photophobia, phonophobia) - Common migraine triggers/symptoms.
  • Associated Symptoms: Photophobia (sensitivity to light) and phonophobia (sensitivity to sound) - Classic migraine symptoms.
  • Associated Symptoms: Nausea and possible emesis (vomiting) - Common migraine symptoms.
  • Aura: Reports visual aura (flashing lights or zigzags) - Strong indicator of migraine with aura.
  • Aura: Reports associated numbness or tingling on one side of the body or face (sensory aura) - Another strong indicator of migraine with aura.
  • Aura Timing: Aura occurs around the same time as the headache, sometimes preceding or concurrent - Typical timing for migraine aura.
  • Pertinent Negatives: Denies fever, chills, neck stiffness - Helps rule out infectious or meningeal causes.
  • Pertinent Negatives: Denies dizziness, loss of balance - Helps rule out vestibular or cerebellar causes.
  • Pertinent Negatives: Denies recent head or neck injury - Rules out traumatic causes.
  • Pertinent Negatives: Denies recent changes in diet or sleep patterns - Rules out some common triggers, though doesn't exclude them entirely.
  • Pertinent Negatives: Denies recent travel - Rules out travel-related infections or exposures.
  • Treatment Response: OTC ibuprofen provides minimal relief - Suggests the headache is severe or not responsive to simple analgesics, common in migraine.
  • Relevant Medical History: Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2 - Important context for overall health and potential medication interactions.
  • Medications: Metformin - Relevant for potential interactions or contraindications.

What wasn't covered but would be helpful:

  • Severity: Pain severity not specified (e.g., scale of 1-10) - Crucial for assessing impact and guiding treatment.
  • Duration: Duration of individual headache episodes not specified - Important for diagnosis and management.
  • Frequency: Frequency of headaches (how often they occur) not specified - Key for classifying migraine type (episodic vs. chronic).
  • Triggers: Specific triggers identified (e.g., stress, certain foods, weather changes, hormonal changes) - Helpful for patient education and prevention.
  • Family History: Family history of headaches, particularly migraine - Migraine often has a genetic component.
  • Past Headache History: Patient denies *similar* headaches, but clarification on *any* past headaches (even different types) would be useful.
  • Neurological Exam Findings: Although not part of the pre-visit report, the *absence* of mention of a neurological exam is a critical missing piece for the PCP's assessment.
  • Impact on Function: How the headache impacts daily activities (work, school, social life) - Helps determine severity and need for treatment.
  • Associated Symptoms (Detailed): Further detail on nausea/vomiting (frequency, severity).
  • Aura Details: Duration of aura symptoms, specific characteristics (e.g., scintillating scotoma, fortification spectra).
  • Other Associated Symptoms: Any associated symptoms like osmophobia (aversion to smells), allodynia (pain from non-painful stimuli), or neck pain.
  • Review of Systems: A broader review of systems might reveal other contributing factors or rule out other conditions.
